Counsel for Opposite Party :- Umesh Kumar,G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Rajiv Kumar Tripathi, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Umesh Kumar, learned counsel for the informant and Sri Sunil Kumar, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as perused the record.
3.

The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in Session Case No.715 of 2024 (State vs. Luv Kush Sen) arising out of Case Crime No.230 of 2024 registered under Sections 376, 323 IPC and 5/6 POCSO Act at Police Station- Bisanda, District Banda with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: As per prosecution story, the applicant is stated to have established corporeal relationship with the informant since 2011 on the false promise of marriage and had subsequently refused to comply with the said betrothal.
In the meantime, the informant is stated to have got her miscarriage conducted several times and even she is stated to have given birth to a son out of the said corporeal relationship.

5. The informant is sated to have married elsewhere in the year 2018, but the said relationship continued.
6.
Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He has nothing to do with the said offence.
The victim is a consenting party.

The bone of contention is that the applicant was subsequently got a government job, but it was not possible for him whatsoever to marry the informant as she was already married elsewhere, which is an admitted fact.
Learned counsel has further stated that the case does not fall within the purview of Section 376 I.P.C. and POCSO Act.
The case to the maximum may fall under Section 494 I.P.C., which is bailable.
7. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
There are no criminal antecedents of the applicant.
The applicant has apprehension of his arrest.

Learned counsel for the applicant undertakes that he has co-operated in the investigation and is ready to do so in trial also failing which the State can move appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail.

8. Per contra, learned counsel for the informant and learned A.G.A. have vehemently opposed the anticipatory bail application but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant.

9. The Supreme Court in Pramod Suryabhan Pawar vs. State of Maharashtra and Another, 2019 (9)
SCC 608 and Ansaar Mohammad vs. State of Rajasthan and Another, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 886, has stated that entering into any kind of corporeal relationship with a person on the false promise to marry cannot be termed as rape.

On due consideration to the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and considering the nature of accusations and antecedents of the applicant, the applicant is liable to be enlarged on anticipatory bail in view of the judgment of Supreme Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1".

sentences.text: The future contingencies regarding the anticipatory bail being granted to applicant shall also be taken care of as per the aforesaid judgment of theSupreme Court.
11. In view of the above, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.

Let the accused-applicant- Luv Kush Sen be released forthwith in the aforesaid case crime (supra) on anticipatory bail till the conclusion of trial on furnishing a personal and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
